subject: Activation plan: model suite & token bands

Cc: Miguel Torres <miguel.torres@aureliahealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Activation plan kickoff

Hi David,

Thanks for the kickoff note. Attached is a quick export of our current product usage (initial_token_profile.xlsx) — it has a 30-day sample with average session length, median turns, and a rough split between search-style prompts and long-context summarization flows.

A few clarifying points from our side:
- Primary use case is document summarization + Q&A over clinical guidelines (average doc length ~18k chars).
- We expect the first cohort to be ~1,200 monthly active users (MAU) and a staged ramp to 10k MAU over 6 months.
- Typical session is 3–8 turns; about 20% of sessions include a long-context chunking step where we pass a 10–12k token history.

Can your team propose a model suite that balances cost and fidelity for both short chat flows and occasional 32k-context jobs? Also please call out concurrency and whether we should plan Dedicated capacity.

Thanks — happy to hop on a call.

— Sara
Product Lead, Aurelia Health

Sara — thanks for the profile and the clear constraints. Monica, Ben, Grace — looping you in to align on a concise proposal for model candidates + token bands.

Quick answers to Sara's asks:
- Yes, we can support multi-length workloads; recommended approach is a small ensemble: one lower-cost 8k model for standard chat, and one higher-context 32k-variant (quantized where appropriate) for doc summarization.
- For 1.2k MAU staging to 10k, we'll sketch both Hosted (pay-as-you-go) and Dedicated (reserved pool) options with projected token spend.

I'll hold a 30-minute sync Thursday if that works — Monica will draft the model suite and a first-pass token band table.

Best,
David
Head of CS, Redwood Inference

From: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Model suite & token bands — first pass

Team / Aurelia — first-pass proposal attached (model_suite_proposal.csv). Key points below: please review and flag anything missing.

Model suite (recommended):
- Tier A (short flows): Redwood-Chat-8k (quantized fp16) — faster, lower cost; good for 80% of sessions.
- Tier B (long-context): Redwood-Long-32k (int8 quantized) — optimized KV cache, chunked summarization pipeline.
- Tier C (quality-critical / fallback): Llama-3-13B-Chat (full-precision) — for top-sensitivity scoring or late-stage reranks.

Context needs mapping:
- Interactive chat: 2k–4k tokens typical (median).
- Document summarization breakpoint: 10k–12k tokens to represent a full guideline; use 32k model for combined context + user prompt.

Token bands (monthly estimate, staging -> ramp):
- Stage (1.2k MAU): 0.9M tokens/day -> ~27M tokens/month (mix: 75% short, 25% long chunk jobs).
- Ramp (10k MAU): 7.5M tokens/day -> ~225M tokens/month (same mix).
- Peak day concurrency estimate: 80–120 concurrent requests; long-context jobs dominate memory footprint.

Operational recommendations:
- Prefix/KV caching for repeated guideline lookups (expected to reduce long-context token cost by ~20–30%).
- Batch size targets: short flows target 16 reqs/batch, long-context keep batching conservative to avoid latency >250ms P95.
- For the ramp scenario, recommend starting Hosted with a Dedicated guardrail: reserve a small Dedicated pool (2–4 GPUs with 32k-enabled variant) to guarantee tail latency for long-context jobs.

Attachments: model_suite_proposal.csv (model latency samples, token-cost math), capacity_back_of_envelope.xlsx (back-of-envelope instance counts).

— Monica
Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference

From: grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, david_kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Hoffman <sara.hoffman@aureliahealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Model suite & token bands — capacity notes

Adding a capacity-focused view to Monica's numbers.

Short summary of infrastructure choices (quantified):
- Staging (1.2k MAU, 27M tokens/mo): Hosted-only viable. Expect P95 short-flow latency ~120–160ms on 8k model with batching. No Dedicated required immediately.
- Early ramp (4–6k MAU, ~90–135M tokens/mo): Recommend Dedicated reserve: 2x A100-class GPUs (or equivalent) for the 32k model to keep tail latency <400ms under concurrency spikes.
- Full ramp (10k MAU, 225M tokens/mo): Dedicated pool sizing: 6–8x A100-class equivalents for long-context heavy periods plus autoscaling for short-flow capacity. This assumes 20% long-context jobs by token weight.

Cost-control levers: quantized 32k model for long jobs (int8), prefix caching, and an L2 rerank step to avoid hitting the 32k model on every user action.

Open questions for Aurelia to confirm:
1) What % of sessions must have sub-1s P95 latency vs. acceptable 300–400ms?
2) Are there regulatory constraints that require on-prem/private deployment (impacts Dedicated sizing and network egress)?

I'll add these figures into the mutual action plan draft — will attach an updated capacity sheet.

— Grace
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Miguel Torres <miguel.torres@aureliahealth.com>
To: david_kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Hoffman <sara.hoffman@aureliahealth.com>, monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-16T09:50:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Model suite & token bands — please confirm SLA and pricing view

David/Monica — thanks, the breakdown is helpful. Two quick asks before we lock the mutual action plan:
- Can you provide a Hosted vs Dedicated cost comparison for the Stage and Ramp scenarios (monthly $) including expected token cost and reserved GPU amortization?
- Confirm the SLA for the Dedicated guardrail (target 99.5% uptime, and tail latency SLO for long-context jobs).

Also, on the latency question: we need P95 < 600ms for long-context summarization (not ideal but acceptable) and P95 < 250ms for short chat flows. If Dedicated can reliably provide that tail, we prefer a small Dedicated commitment at ramp.

Miguel
CTO, Aurelia Health
